spec.headline: Cross-Margin Contagion vs. Isolated Containment
spec.subhead: Structural boundaries prevent asset shocks from cascading across portfolio collateral.

blocks.text: Cross-Margin Protocol: A single asset shock drains shared collateral pools, spreading liquidation risk portfolio-wide.
Isolated Architecture: Structural firewalls strictly seal settlement to the distressed position, preserving adjacent capital.

focal.reason: Demonstrates structural containment of liquidation risk to a single account without balance spillover.

defects.issue: Severe bottom-half dead space causing vertical imbalance
defects.location: Bottom 45% of canvas (from y ≈ 620px down to 1080px)
defects.reason: All copy and layout structure are compressed into the top 55% of the frame, leaving the entire lower half completely vacant. This reads as an abandoned or unfinished layout rather than intentional negative space.
defects.fix: Center the content stack vertically on the canvas by increasing the top margin above the logo to 140px and increasing vertical spacing between the subhead and comparison blocks to 72px.

defects.issue: Lack of typographic hierarchy in comparison columns
defects.location: Comparison section columns (left and right text blocks)
defects.reason: Headers ('Cross-Margin Protocol:' and 'Isolated Architecture:') run inline with the body text at the same size and weight, forcing the viewer to read full paragraphs rather than quickly parsing the intended comparison.
defects.fix: Separate 'Cross-Margin Protocol' and 'Isolated Architecture' into distinct subheadings stacked above the body copy, set them in bold or medium weight, and add a 12px margin beneath them before the description text.

defects.reason: The intended focal element relies solely on slightly brighter font color to distinguish itself from the left column, which fails to assert clear visual dominance within 2 seconds.
defects.fix: Encase the right comparison block in a subtle semi-transparent background panel (e.g., 4% white/accent fill with a 1px border at 12% opacity) to anchor it as the preferred structural model.
